prompt:
A cinematic storyboard sheet for a Sri Lankan television drama: 6 photorealistic film stills of ONE scene, laid out in a grid 3 panels across and 2 down, read left to right, then top to bottom. Every panel is a tall portrait 9:16 still of the same size, separated by thin, even, plain white gutters. All panels are the same scene's world, painted together: the same people, props, light and colour grade in every panel. The weather and the ground (dry or wet, rain falling or not) are as each panel says: they can change during the scene, and a panel that says it is dry has no rain and no wet ground.

Reference images, in order: image 1 is the location plate for Colombo roadside; image 2 is the approved last panel of the previous part of this scene's board. Take from image 1: the kind of place: its ground, water, plants, structures and materials. It is ONE view of the place; each panel has its own camera position, so do not repeat this view in every panel; image 2: panel 1 of this sheet, repeated exactly: the same camera, place, light and mannequins.

People (every panel): every person is a smooth, matte, faceless artist's mannequin in one solid colour, with jointed limbs and simple hands: Kasun is the red mannequin; Anudi is the blue mannequin. A small raised ridge on the front of the head, where a nose would be, shows which way the head faces. Each mannequin has the person's real height and build and sits, stands and holds things exactly as a real person would. No faces, no hair, no clothes, no skin: only the mannequin colour. Everything else (the place, the props, the light, the weather) is a real, photorealistic film still.

World (every panel): Paint one unified storyboard image in a four-column, four-row grid, reading left to right and top to bottom. Fill the first fourteen cells and leave the final two cells blank, with plain gutters and no lettering, numbering or arrows anywhere. Use only their poses to convey attention. Render the setting and props realistically: Anudi's orange smartphone has a transparent case matching the reference, her navy folding umbrella is open, and her tan structured handbag has brass-coloured fittings. Throughout the conversation her left hand holds the umbrella shaft at waist height, with the handbag suspended from her left shoulder; her right hand receives and retains the phone. Soft early-morning overcast daylight comes from the road at camera right, balanced around 5600K, with warm naturalistic colour, muted greens and earth tones, and subdued amber shop practicals. The pavement and patched asphalt are wet, with shallow reflections and no falling rain throughout. Keep the business slightly darker than the foreground.

Geography: The narrow concrete pavement forms a continuous left-to-right path between the road in the foreground and weathered commercial frontages behind it. A small, muted leaf-green food three-wheeler occupies the vending bay at the left end, with an open serving hatch, metal counter and shelter canopy. Immediately right of the bay is the conversation position: Kasun stands on its left, Anudi on its right. A pale-green building pier and weathered concrete boundary wall continue behind Anudi toward the open pavement at screen right, her departure direction. The kerb drain follows the pavement across the foreground; utility poles and cables belong to the same connected frontage. All cameras stay on the road-facing side of the conversational axis. Wider views show the business at frame left and the pale-green pier at frame right; tighter views preserve those sides without forcing distant landmarks into their crops.

PANEL 1 (row 1, column 1) — Standing eye height from Kasun's road-facing side, matching the side of shot 7; 85mm close-up, the mannequin's head filling the panel, shallow depth of field. Background: A narrow pale-green blur remains at frame right, with darker frontage blur at frame left. The three-wheeler stays offscreen left; the umbrella shaft is confined to the far-right edge if it enters the crop. The blue mannequin's head fills the panel in a leftward three-quarter orientation, with the upper chest still aligned screen left. Its right hand cups the orange phone against the camera-near side of its head, placing the phone along the frame-right contour. The left hand and handbag are outside the close crop, with the left hand still occupied by the umbrella below frame.
PANEL 2 (row 1, column 2) — Standing eye height from the same road-facing setup as shot 7; 65mm, chest-up medium close-up, shallow depth of field. Background: The pale-green pier returns at frame right and the darker frontage remains frame left. The food business is beyond the left crop, maintaining the single's established orientation. The blue mannequin stands frame right with chest facing left and head inclined slightly down-left in three-quarter view. Its right hand holds the phone against the camera-near side of its head, along the frame-right contour, with the bent forearm visible. Its left hand remains below the crop on the umbrella shaft, which rises at the far-right side of the torso. The handbag strap remains over the far shoulder.
PANEL 3 (row 1, column 3) — Standing eye height from the original road-facing master position; 40mm, waist-up two-shot, both mannequins and handset sharp. Background: The food three-wheeler and serving counter return clearly at frame left behind the red mannequin. The pale-green pier and concrete wall remain frame right behind the blue mannequin. The red mannequin stands left, chest facing right and head directed toward the blue mannequin's lowered head, with both empty hands at its sides. The blue mannequin stands right, chest facing left and head angled down toward the phone held screen-up at chest height. Its camera-near right hand supports the phone with the thumb poised beside the display, before any visible touch. Its far left hand holds the umbrella shaft at waist height beside the frame-right edge of its torso, and the handbag hangs over its far hip.
PANEL 4 (row 2, column 1) — Standing eye height from the same road-facing close two-shot setup as shot 5; 65mm, close chest-up shared frame, both heads sharp. Background: The softly blurred food hatch remains frame left behind the red mannequin. The pale-green pier remains frame right behind the blue mannequin. The red mannequin stands left with chest facing right and head turned toward the blue mannequin. The blue mannequin stands right with chest facing left and head turned toward the red mannequin, both held in readable three-quarter orientations. The red hands remain empty below the crop; the blue right hand holds the phone below the crop and its left hand holds the umbrella shaft. The shaft and far-shoulder handbag strap remain along the blue silhouette's frame-right edge.
PANEL 5 (row 2, column 2) — Standing eye height from the same closer road-facing setup as shots 2 and 4; 50mm, chest-up two-shot, medium depth of field. Background: The recognizable business hatch stays frame left. The pale-green pier and the beginning of the rightward pavement frontage stay frame right. The red mannequin stands frame left with chest facing right and head directed toward the blue mannequin in three-quarter profile. The blue mannequin stands frame right with chest facing left and head directed toward the red mannequin. Both red hands rest below the crop, while the blue right hand retains the phone at waist height below frame and its left hand holds the umbrella shaft. The umbrella shaft and handbag strap remain on the far side of the blue body, along its frame-right edge.
PANEL 6 (row 2, column 3) — Standing eye height farther back on the road-facing side; 35mm wide shot showing both full figures, the vending bay and the lateral exit path, deep depth of field. Background: The complete food three-wheeler occupies frame left, with its serving hatch, canopy and amber shop opening behind it. The same pale-green pier and weathered boundary wall continue across frame right beside the unobstructed pavement; the kerb drain and patched road run across the foreground. The red mannequin stands frame left, chest and head facing right toward the blue mannequin, with both empty hands hanging at its sides. The blue mannequin stands frame right at the start of departure, chest and head oriented screen right in lateral three-quarter profile, feet still planted rather than already mid-stride. Its right hand holds the phone low on the far side of its body, partly concealed, while its left hand holds the open umbrella on the camera-near side. Its handbag hangs from the near left shoulder over the near hip, along the lower-left edge of its silhouette, leaving clear pavement ahead toward screen right.

Bodies (every panel): each person sits or stands the way a real person does the task in front of them, never posed for the camera. The body faces the task and only the head turns: someone at a steering wheel sits squarely behind it, the wheel centred in front of the chest, back against the seat, both hands on the rim; someone at a desk sits square to it; someone at a stove faces the stove. A camera beside a person sees the body side-on, not the chest. Nobody looks into or faces the lens unless the panel says so. Head and eyes turn together: the eyes never roll hard to one side while the face points at the camera; a near-frontal face looks just past the lens.

Draw NO text of any kind: no panel numbers, no captions, no titles, no timestamps, no arrows, no labels, no borders other than the gutters. The people, place and everyday details are Sri Lankan.

conflicts: The mannequin instruction replaces the human appearance references and prevents visible speaking or expression details; the board uses body and head orientation instead.
Shot 6 requests exact caller-identification text, but the board prohibits all written text. Its screen therefore shows an incoming-call layout without lettering.
Several script-line assignments anticipate later actions, especially in shots 5, 8 and 10. The panels follow the specified opening pictures rather than advancing to those later actions.
Shot 5 refers to an unspecified L9 in its action notes but supplies no spoken line. No dialogue or additional action has been invented.
The location description mixes early-morning daylight with evening shop light. The board follows the shot plans' overcast daylight and retains amber shop practicals.
Anudi's reference picture shows a folded umbrella, while her scene condition requires it open. The umbrella is open throughout this board.
The plan requests facial detail that the approved smooth, faceless mannequin treatment cannot show; the panel preserves the opening head pose and handset position.
